#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  You play $DUSK  nodes: roll the interest you’ve earned directly into an older position—almost everyone defaults to this kind of move. @Dusk_Foundation ’s proposed plan sounds great at first glance: instead of starting a new node and waiting 6 to 12 hours, just add to the old pool. Suppose you top up with 10,000 tokens: 9,000 tokens can instantly enter the active state to mine, while the remaining 1,000 tokens become locked. You sacrifice 10% liquidity to get 90% of your funds working immediately—on the face of it, you’re definitely not losing.

But long-term players quickly discover the hidden reefs. The key issue is the “reinvestment frequency.” Every time you roll profits back in, the system will consistently skim off one-tenth and lock it as a stagnant state. That money is still under your name, but it produces zero returns. Stretch the timeline out: if you add a total of 100,000 tokens in batches, roughly 10,000 tokens will gradually turn into “dead chips.” When you calculate your real return rate, that capital tied up and locked away will drag down your overall profits severely.

Even more tormenting is that retrieving these idle, stuck assets is quite cumbersome. According to the official instructions, when certain conditions occur, you must take the entire node’s chips out as a whole—everything—then fully unbind. Unbinding is fast, but if you want to start staking for yield again, the entire position has to go through that same 6 to 12 hour queue just to reactivate. In other words, the time you carefully squeezed out day-to-day through reinvestment ends up being given back when you finally reorganize the holdings—and during that period, the account’s earnings basically drop to zero.

Once you understand this mechanism, you realize the rule is a double-edged sword. Forcing locked shares does indeed reduce some immediate sell pressure, but it contributes nothing to on-chain consensus security. And if major node operators collectively pull back to activate idle funds, a large amount of chips will temporarily return to the liquid market. So don’t let long-term investors be fooled by an inflated “total staking rate.” Focus on the true proportion of active chips, the size of idle locked funds, and how often big players queue to reorganize—only then can you see whether this compounding game is truly generating returns for you, or effectively trapping your principal.#eth $ETH

然而，长线玩家很快就会摸到其中的暗礁。症结就在“加仓频率”上。你每一次把利润复投，系统都会雷打不动地截留十分之一作为停滞状态。这笔钱虽在你名下，却无法产生任何收益。拉长周期看，假如你分批追加了累计10万枚，不知不觉就有约1万枚沦为了“死筹码”。核算真实回报率时，这笔被占压的本金会把你的总体利润狠狠拉低。

更折磨人的是，想把这笔趴窝的资产捞出来，流程相当繁杂。按官方提示，遇到特定情况你必须把整个节点的筹码连锅端，全部解绑。解绑固然快，可一旦想再次质押生息，全仓资金又得重新去熬那6到12小时的排队激活。等于说，你靠日常复投精打细算抠出来的时间，在最终重组仓位时全吐了回去，期间整个账户的收益彻底挂零。

搞懂这套玩法就知道，该规则对盘面是把双刃剑。强制 locked 的份额确实锁死了部分抛压，但对链上共识安全毫无贡献。并且，一旦大节点为了盘活闲钱集体退仓，大量筹码会短暂重返流通市场。所以，长线投资别被虚高的“总质押率”忽悠了。盯紧 active 筹码的真实占比、闲置 locked 的体量，以及大户重组排队的频率，才能看透这场复利游戏到底是在替你创收，还是在变相圈禁你的本金。#eth $ETH

【If ETH drops another 200 yuan, how many people would die in the market】

Honestly, recently I’ve been getting private messages from people in the background asking me whether they can still hold ETH. I don’t know how to answer, either. Why? Because I’m not sure myself.

Right now the chart is basically one word: chop. At $ 1880, it’s neither up nor down. In the past 24 hours it’s only down 0.6%, and over a week it’s down just 1%. It doesn’t look painful, right? But the problem is exactly here—trading volume is incredibly low. Everyone is waiting. Waiting for what? Waiting for someone else to move first.

FNG is 29, and the weekly average is also 29. What does this indicate? It means panic hasn’t worsened further, but don’t expect anyone to be bold enough to buy the dip. Market sentiment right now is like a tamed animal—everyone is scared to move, because they’ve already been traumatized by the huge bull-and-bear swings of 2021.

BTC dominance is still at 56.2%, standing there like it owns the place. The “big brother” behavior of pooling funds hasn’t changed. ETH may have opportunities, but the funds simply aren’t going. In this kind of setup, can ETH independently move up strongly? Hard to say.

Some people will say Goldman Sachs acquiring NEOS is a positive. Sure, let’s call it a positive. But I want to ask: for this $2.25B acquisition, what exactly will it do for ETH holders? Will the ETF size increase? Okay. Then what—trading fees go down? Or annualized returns go up? Honestly, large institutions’ positioning is based on long-term logic. They can’t control the short-term market.

Bitmine’s 257M annualized staking income is similar. It sounds impressive, but that’s the institution’s business. What does it have to do with you, a small retail investor who actually holds a position?

Right now, when I look at ETH, I’m basically watching. $ 1850 is support. If it breaks, then $ 1750 is next. Resistance? $ 1950. Getting there in the short term won’t be easy. The direction is close to being decided, but unless volume increases, I’d rather not move.

What’s your mindset right now? If you have a position, are you going to hold on for dear life, or did you trim? If you’re in cash with no position—would you dare to enter around here? Anyway, what I say doesn’t matter. After I finish talking, if you’re itchy, you’ll still be itchy.

The S&P 500 closes at a new all-time high again

The performance of U.S. benchmark indexes has once again become a focal point for global risk assets. According to compiled financial information, the S&P 500 closed at a new all-time high in the latest trading session. The result was quickly discussed by the market and incorporated into a framework for monitoring macro sentiment.

In terms of background, the S&P 500—widely seen as the key gauge of the overall performance of large U.S. listed companies—has long been regarded as an important barometer of global risk appetite. Its constituents span multiple heavily weighted sectors, including technology, consumer, financials, and industrials. Whether the index can continue to set fresh records at elevated levels often reflects the market’s combined pricing of expectations for economic growth, the resilience of corporate earnings, and the prevailing liquidity environment. When the index breaks to new highs at the close rather than only intraday, it typically suggests that buy-side strength has been relatively dominant throughout the trading day, making the closing price a more representative measure.

On the core facts, what can currently be confirmed is this: the S&P 500 closed at a new all-time high. Public materials highlighted it as one of the day’s key financial items. It should be noted that the existing evidence mainly confirms the outcome itself—“closing at a new high”—without fully disclosing the specific closing level, the contribution by each sector, changes in trading value, or the precise percentage difference versus the prior peak. Therefore, it would be inappropriate to overextend conclusions into the fine-driving details. Other macro variables mentioned alongside the index include long-end U.S. Treasury yields, exchange rates, and commodity prices; however, the evidence does not provide a verifiable, quantified breakdown of their causal weight relative to the S&P 500’s new high. They can only be treated as parallel items to observe.

As for the logic behind index closing at a new high, it usually carries several implications. First, a rebalancing of earnings and valuation: if leading companies’ earnings reports and forward guidance are steady, the index is more likely to rise under the influence of heavy-weight stocks. Second, a repricing of liquidity and rate expectations: when the market believes the policy path can still be matched to the pricing of risk assets, the resistance to further index highs may relatively decline. Third, confirmation from fund-flow behavior: a closing-price break tends to reflect the combined effect of institutional positioning and passive capital more than an intraday surge. At the same time, it’s important to recognize the other side: a new index high does not automatically mean the market’s internal structure is healthy. If the rally is concentrated in a handful of heavy weights and breadth is lacking, or if volatility and trading activity do not expand in tandem, the new high more likely reflects “strength at the index level” rather than a broad-based advance. In the absence of simultaneous breadth data and detailed fund-flow information, the above structural assessment can only serve as a framework-level prompt, not a confirmed conclusion.

The transmission path to the crypto market is more about the propagation of risk appetite rather than a one-to-one, immediate mapping. Traditionally, when U.S. stocks—especially benchmark indexes like the S&P 500—strengthen, market risk appetite often improves. Some capital may become more tolerant of high-volatility assets, allowing crypto assets to benefit indirectly from a rebound in risk sentiment. When technology growth styles lead, the market is also more likely to link liquidity-loosening expectations with growth narratives, creating a sentiment-level resonance in crypto pricing. Conversely, if a new stock index high coincides with a significant rise in Treasury yields, a stronger U.S. dollar, or repeated swings in liquidity expectations, risk assets internally could see a “stocks strong, coins diverge” scenario. Based on the evidence available today, what can be confirmed is the macro backdrop of the benchmark U.S. index closing at a new high. Whether the crypto market also increases in volume, and which sectors are more sensitive, still depends on subsequent liquidity, regulation, and event-driven factors—it cannot be directly extrapolated from a single index outcome.

The editorial takeaway and observation is: it is more appropriate to understand “the S&P 500 closing at a new historical high” as a set of macro sentiment signals, rather than as a single trading instruction. For observers of crypto and other risk assets, more value lies in tracking the quality of confirmation after the new high— including the depth of pullbacks, whether trading activity keeps pace, whether interest rates and the U.S. dollar form hedging pressure, and whether the linkages between risk assets remain stable. At the factual level, currently only the index closing at a refreshed historical peak can be confirmed. Whether the rally is sustainable and whether it will create a continued spillover into the crypto market remains speculative and requires later data verification. Overall, this event strengthens the narrative that “global risk assets continue to price growth and liquidity at elevated levels,” but it also serves as a reminder: a new high is not the endpoint—structure and constraint conditions are equally critical.

content:
美股标普500指数收盘再创历史新高

美股基准指数走势再度成为全球风险资产关注焦点。据相关财经汇总信息，标普500指数在最新交易中收盘创下历史新高，这一结果迅速被市场讨论并纳入宏观情绪观察框架。

从事件背景看，标普500指数作为衡量美国大型上市公司整体表现的核心指标，长期被视作全球风险偏好的重要风向标。其成分覆盖科技、消费、金融、工业等多个权重板块，指数能否在高位继续刷新纪录，往往对应着资金对经济增长预期、企业盈利韧性以及流动性环境的综合定价。当指数以收盘价而非仅盘中价刷新高点时，通常意味着多头力量在全天交易中占据相对主导，收盘定价更具代表性。

核心事实方面，目前可确认的信息是：标普500指数收盘创历史新高。公开材料将其作为当日财经要点之一予以强调。需要说明的是，现有证据主要确认“收盘创新高”这一结果本身，并未完整披露具体收盘点位、分板块贡献、成交额变化，以及与前高之间的精确幅度；因此，对驱动细节不宜过度延伸。与指数同步被提及的，还有美债长端收益率、汇率与商品价格等宏观变量，但它们与本次标普创新高之间的因果权重，证据并未给出可核验的量化拆解，只能作为并列观察项。

逻辑拆解上，指数收盘创新高通常包含几层含义。其一，是盈利与估值的再平衡：若龙头公司财报与前瞻指引偏稳，指数更容易在权重股带动下抬升；其二，是流动性与利率预期的再定价：当市场认为政策路径尚可匹配风险资产定价时，股指冲高的阻力会相对下降；其三，是资金行为层面的确认，收盘价刷新往往比盘中冲高更能反映机构仓位与被动资金的共同作用。但也要看到另一面：指数新高并不自动等于市场内部结构健康，若上涨集中在少数权重、广度不足，或波动率与成交并未同步放大，则新高更多体现“指数层面的强”，而非“全面普涨”。在缺少同步广度与资金流向明细的情况下，上述结构判断只能作为框架性提示，而非已证实结论。

对加密市场的影响路径，更多体现为风险偏好的传导，而非一一对应的即时映射。传统上，当美股尤其是标普等基准指数走强时，市场风险胃口往往改善，部分资金对高波动资产的容忍度上升，加密资产可能间接受益于风险情绪回暖；科技成长风格占优时，市场也更容易把流动性宽松预期与成长叙事联系起来，从而对加密定价形成情绪层面的共振。反过来，若股指新高伴随美债收益率显著抬升、美元走强或流动性预期反复，则风险资产内部可能出现“股强而币分化”的局面。就当前证据而言，能够确认的是美股基准指数收盘创新高这一宏观背景，加密市场是否同步放量、哪些板块更敏感，仍取决于后续流动性、监管与事件驱动，不能由单一股指结果直接外推。

编辑判断与观察是：把“标普500收盘历史新高”理解为一组宏观情绪信号，比理解成单一交易指令更合适。对加密与风险资产观察者而言，更有价值的是跟踪新高之后的确认质量——包括回撤幅度、成交是否跟上、利率与美元是否形成对冲压力，以及风险资产之间的联动是否稳定。事实层面，目前仅能确认指数收盘刷新历史高点；关于上涨是否可持续、会否向加密市场形成持续溢出，仍属推测，需要后续数据验证。整体上，这一事件强化了“全球风险资产仍在高位定价增长与流动性”的叙事，但也提醒市场：新高本身不是终点，结构与约束条件同样关键。

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  On Friday, I翻了翻 the core source code of Dusk ($DUSK) consensus.rs. Objectively speaking, its three-layer verification mechanism paired with the Kadcast protocol—claimed to save half the traffic—really is impressive in terms of architectural ideas. But when I focused on the variable EMERGENCY_MODE_ITERATION_THRESHOLD, my confidence instantly dropped.

This so-called “emergency mode” is supposed to be a safety cushion when the system lags, but the source code doesn’t clearly explain what the actual trigger threshold is. In a crisis, who packages those special blocks, and what exactly are the validation criteria? Official documentation is completely clueless. This kind of black-box setting, once deployed on the mainnet, is extremely easy for hackers to maliciously target.

Go check Issue #1907 and you’ll find that this logic was already criticized by peers long ago. With the current code, as soon as the iteration count runs out, the counter is blindly reset to zero and the process is restarted. That means the worse the network environment is, the more nodes will spin in place going nowhere. Even though the community suggested optimizing it into a “state suspend,” nothing has ever been implemented—talk without practice.

What really makes your scalp tingle is Issue #2361. Imagine: if a large number of nodes simultaneously fall behind and collectively switch into emergency mode, the system will drive them to instantly send GetBlocks requests in perfect synchrony. With no rate limiting and no buffering—this was intended as self-rescue, but it directly turns into a DDoS attack that knocks its own mainnet over, instantly exhausting bandwidth.

And then, on top of Kadcast’s underwhelming performance, it’s even more disastrous. In early tests with very small scale, even broadcasting couldn’t achieve 100% coverage. Dusk is highly dependent on multi-round node confirmations; if a single packet gets lost, consensus is likely to time out. Once it times out, it triggers that emergency mode full of traps again—an vicious cycle born right there.

All things considered, at its current stage, Dusk’s mechanism is far from a secure foundation; instead, it feels more like a mine that could explode at any time. #eth $ETH

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  周五翻了翻 Dusk ($DUSK) 的核心源码 consensus.rs。客观讲，它的三层验证机制搭配号称能省一半流量的 Kadcast 协议，架构构思确实惊艳。但当我盯上 EMERGENCY_MODE_ITERATION_THRESHOLD 这个变量时，心里瞬间没底了。

这个“紧急模式”本该是系统卡顿时的安全垫，但源码里根本没交待清楚触发底线是多少。危机时特殊区块由谁打包、校验标准是什么？官方资料毫无头绪。这种黑盒设定，一旦上主网极易被黑客恶意针对。

去翻翻 Issue #1907 就会发现，这套逻辑早就被同行吐槽了。按现有代码，只要迭代次数耗尽，计数器就无脑清零重跑。这意味着网络环境越差，节点越是原地疯狂空转。虽然社区建议优化成“状态挂起”，但一直没见落地，光说不练。

真正让人头皮发麻的是 Issue #2361。试想，如果大批节点同时掉队并集体切进紧急状态，系统会驱使它们瞬间齐刷刷地发送 GetBlocks 请求。毫无限流和缓冲，这本意是自救，结果直接演变成了搞垮自家主网的 DDoS 攻击，瞬间榨干带宽。

再叠加上 Kadcast 协议的拉胯表现，就更要命了。早期极小规模的测试中，发个广播都无法做到百分百覆盖。Dusk 可是高度依赖多轮节点确认的，底层一丢包，共识就容易超时；一超时，又去触发那个到处是坑的紧急模式，恶性循环就此诞生。

盘点下来，Dusk 现阶段这套机制离安全底座相去甚远，反而更像是个随时会自爆的雷。#eth $ETH

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  A few days ago I took some time to look into Dusk’s backend code (mainly consensus.rs). Honestly, the SA consensus mechanism described in their whitepaper is pretty interesting: proposals, validation, and confirmation are handled by three different node committees. They also claim that Kadcast can save half the traffic for transmission. But when I saw the parameter EMERGENCY_MODE_ITERATION_THRESHOLD, I felt uneasy. This so-called “emergency fallback” doesn’t seem as reliable as the宣传 makes it out to be. Even the triggering conditions, emergency block production, and validation logic are all unclear—there’s not even a trace of it in the public documentation.

Digging through their GitHub history is even more striking—this part had already been raised as an Issue. For example, #1907 pointed out that after nodes time out in the last round of block production, the counter simply gets reset and they rerun. That means once the network gets bad, nodes will just get stuck in this dead loop, hard-working at it over and over. The community previously discussed changing it to “pause and keep state while stuck,” but so far the code still hasn’t changed, and handling of edge cases is quite rough.

By the time you get to Issue #2361, it gets even worse. Suppose there’s widespread disconnect on-chain and all network nodes are forced into emergency mode together. The result is that everyone simultaneously spams the whole network with GetBlocks requests to pull data. Because the necessary request rate-limiting mechanism is missing, what was originally meant to prevent deadlock turns into a traffic bombing against their own mainnet—instantly exhausting all bandwidth.

And looking at the underlying Kadcast: when they previously tested at small scale with 10 nodes, the messages still couldn’t be broadcast to everyone. Public chains like Dusk rely on frequent packet exchanges among committees to run consensus. If broadcasts miss packets, consensus times out; once it times out, it repeatedly collides with that immature emergency mode, and all kinds of risks end up stringing together like a fuse.

In my view, once Dusk’s unfinished emergency mode ($DUSK) is deployed on the real mainnet, it’s likely not a cure, but a hidden risk introduced into the system. I hope the team can fill in the underlying broadcasting and add proper request rate-limiting as soon as possible. #eth $ETH

content:
#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  前几天抽空研究了下 Dusk 的后端代码（主要是 consensus.rs 那块）。讲真，他们白皮书里写的那套 SA 共识机制挺有意思，搞了提案、校验和确认三个不同的节点委员会，再加上 Kadcast 说是能给传输省下一半流量。但等我看到 EMERGENCY_MODE_ITERATION_THRESHOLD 这行参数时，心里就有点打鼓了。这所谓的“紧急兜底”根本不像宣传的那么靠谱，连触发条件、应急出块和验证逻辑都是糊涂账，公开文档里连字影都没有。

去翻他们的 GitHub 记录更刺眼，这部分其实早被发了 Issue。比如 #1907 就指出来：现在节点在最后一轮出块超时后，计数器会直接清零重跑。这意味着一旦遇到糟糕的网络，节点只会卡在这个死循环里硬折腾。社区之前讨论说要改成“卡住挂起保持状态”，但至今代码里依然没动静，边缘状况下的处理相当粗糙。

到了 Issue #2361，问题就更严重了。假设链上出现了大面积掉线，全网节点被迫一起进紧急模式，结果就是大家同时向全网狂发 GetBlocks 请求拉数据。因为缺了必要的请求限速机制，这套原本用来防卡死的回退机制，反而会秒变针对自己主网的流量轰炸，瞬间把所有带宽吃干抹净。

再看看底层的 Kadcast，其实之前小规模跑 10 个节点测试时，消息都没法做到全员播发。Dusk 这类公链是全靠委员会频繁发包交互来跑共识的，广播只要漏包，共识就得超时；一超时就频繁撞上那套不成熟的紧急模式，各种隐患直接串成了一根引线。

在我看来，Dusk（$DUSK）这个未完工的紧急模式一旦上了真实主网，很可能不是解药，而是给系统埋下了隐患。希望团队能尽快把底层的广播和请求限速补齐吧。#eth $ETH

title: 🔄 八年研究、数千万美元打水漂？以太坊基金会正式放弃L1的Poseidon哈希
subTitle:
#以太坊基金会L1弃用Poseidon哈希 
8月13日，以太坊基金会研究员Justin Drake在X平台发文宣布：以太坊基金会决定在L1层放弃Poseidon哈希函数，转向SHA或BLAKE等传统哈希函数。
这一决定结束了自2018年以来长达八年、耗资数千万美元的后量子密码学探索。
🔍 Poseidon是什么？为什么放弃？
Poseidon是2019年诞生的“SNARK友好型”哈希函数，专为零知识证明系统优化设计，被大量zkRollup和zkVM使用，保障着数十亿美元级别的资产安全。
放弃的核心原因不是Poseidon本身出了问题，而是SNARK设计取得了突破性进展：
· 通过 “二进制域”（binary field） 运算方式，传统哈希函数（SHA/BLAKE）在SNARK电路中的性能已可媲美Poseidon
· 单台笔记本电脑每秒可完成约100万次传统哈希调用验证，仅有约100倍的CPU开销
· 范式从“为SNARK优化哈希”转向了 “为哈希优化SNARK” 
⚠️ 另一个关键因素：安全性
随着AI密码分析能力的提升，部分后量子密码方案近期相继遭受攻击——格密码方案HAWK和同源密码方案SQIsign均出现安全挫折。
相比之下，SHA和BLAKE这类经过数十年审查的传统哈希函数，已知攻击向量更少，部署速度可能更快。以太坊基金会甚至专门启动了100万美元的Poseidon密码分析计划来压力测试，最终仍倾向于更成熟的替代方案。
📅 后续时间线：
· 2027年：推出生产级leanVM
· 2028年：部署到以太坊的共识层、数据层和执行层
Justin Drake表示，这些日期仍属初步计划。
🔗 对相关代币的可能影响：
· $ETH：决策本身对以太坊长期安全架构是利好——转向经过数十年验证的传统哈希，后量子抗性更明确。但短期内属技术面调整，对ETH价格直接影响有限。
· ZK赛道代币（$ZK、$STRK等）：Poseidon被L1放弃，但Drake明确表示Poseidon目前仍通过zkRollup和zkVM保障着数十亿级别资产。对已部署的ZK项目暂无直接影响，但新项目可能会重新评估哈希方案选择。
· AI/Crypto交叉概念：AI密码分析能力的提升加速了此次决策，这一逻辑可能被市场短期炒作。
💡 怎么看？
这是一次罕见的 “技术路线大转向” ——以太坊基金会花了八年时间、数千万美元押注Poseidon，最终因为SNARK技术本身进步太快而主动放弃。传统哈希在ZK电路里跑出了接近Poseidon的性能，再加上数十年安全审计积累的信任优势，Poseidon的“专属优势”消失了。
有时候，最好的创新不是发明新东西，而是让旧东西变得足够好。
投资有风险，决策需谨慎。本文仅作信息分享，不构成任何投资建议。
---

translatedData.subTitle:
<t-99/>#以太坊基金会L1弃用Poseidon哈希 
On August 13, Justin Drake, a researcher at the Ethereum Foundation, posted on the X platform announcing that the Ethereum Foundation has decided to abandon the Poseidon hash function on the L1 layer and move to traditional hash functions such as SHA or BLAKE.
This decision ends the eight-year, multi-hundred-million-dollar exploration of post-quantum cryptography that began in 2018.
🔍 What is Poseidon? Why was it abandoned?
Poseidon is a “SNARK-friendly” hash function created in 2019, optimized specifically for zero-knowledge proof systems. It is widely used by zkRollups and zkVMs, helping to ensure the security of assets worth billions of dollars.

Position sizing needs to differentiate between spot and contracts. title: Crypto Market Update: Bitcoin Range Persists as SEC Delay, ETF Flows and Tokenization Drive Sentiment
subTitle:
Bitcoin remains range-bound as traders weigh U.S. policy, ETF flows and security headlines. CoinDesk reported that BTC has spent weeks around a $62,000 to $66,000 range, with ETF buying offset by miner and corporate-holder selling while volatility stays low. The latest tone is cautious rather than deeply bearish: the market has support, but it still lacks the volume needed for a convincing breakout.

Regulation is the dominant macro story. Investor's Business Daily reported that the SEC and OCC are still moving crypto policy forward even as the Senate delays the CLARITY Act until after recess. The SEC's broader Regulation Crypto agenda and the OCC's openness to crypto-related bank charters point to a more formal market structure, but not instant clarity. That uncertainty can keep capital selective.

ETF flows are another pressure point. CoinStats noted that U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF flows flipped negative by about $61.1 million on August 12, while ETH ETFs stayed modestly positive. This does not erase the institutional story, but it does mean bulls need renewed inflows to keep defending the range.

The Block's latest feed also highlights two themes to watch: Bitwise exploring tokenization of its Solana staking ETF through Superstate, and Tether receiving a clean KPMG opinion in its first full audit. Tokenization and stablecoin transparency both remain key institutional narratives.

For traders, the playbook remains patient. BTC, ETH and liquid altcoins may react sharply to policy and ETF headlines, but sustained trend needs stronger volume, renewed flows and cleaner regulatory signals. #BTC #ETH #Crypto #ETF #Macro

【If ETH breaks below 1700, what the big players do is more interesting than the price itself】

Let’s talk about a few on-chain signals from this week.

First, the news about Goldman Sachs acquiring NEOS—its $ 30 billion deal involves an ETF business, and ETH-related products are included as well. Institutions are putting real money on the table, which is more substantive than just slogans. But the question is—if institutions come in, can ETH automatically go up? Back in 2017, institutions were still watching from the sidelines. That didn’t stop prices from rising—or falling. So when I read this news, my takeaway is simple: someone is planning, but planning and “harvesting” are two different things.

What’s truly interesting are several signals revealed by on-chain data.

The ETH holdings in the wallets of big players have been quietly increasing, while retail holders are running out. I’ve seen this playbook before—early 2021 was exactly like this. Once the concentration of big players’ chips rises, the next move is usually either a burst of momentum or a sign that the main forces are preparing to distribute. At this point, we can’t tell which yet, but one thing is certain: it isn’t retail buying.

Exchange net flows have recently leaned toward inflows, suggesting that someone is preparing to sell. Coupled with subdued trading volume, it also hints that market sentiment is cautious—before deciding on a direction, everyone is waiting.

Active addresses are declining, but the number of addresses holding for more than a year is rising. Put together, this is pretty intriguing: short-term participants are withdrawing, while long-term holders are waiting. This looks like market rotation, not outright selling.

On valuation: $ 1872 is only one step away from key support at $ 1825. Right now, the market sentiment “FNG” is 29, which sits at the edge of the extreme panic zone. Valuation being low is true, but undervaluation doesn’t automatically mean an immediate rally. In the second half of 2018, valuations were also low, yet prices still drifted lower for half a year.

Honestly, what I care about now is whether Goldman’s acquisition can translate into real business expansion for ETH. If the ETF scale really gets going, that would be the big-picture logic that benefits ETH as well. But if it’s only financial-layer M&A integration, the short-term impact is likely limited.

In practice, it comes down to whether institutional ETF products can truly attract money to flow in. It’s still early, so I won’t make a conclusion yet.

What’s everyone’s mindset right now? Do you want to add here, or are you looking to run? Are you getting itchy?

【如果ETH跌破1700，大户们的反应比价格本身更有意思】

说说链上这周的几个信号。

先说高盛收购NEOS这件事$ 30亿的ETF业务，ETH相关产品也在里面。机构在用真金白银表态，这比喊口号实在。但问题是——机构进来了，ETH就能涨吗？2017年那会儿机构还在观望呢，不耽误涨也不耽误跌。所以这条消息我看完就一个感受：有人在布局，但布局和收割是两回事。

真正有意思的是链上数据透出来的几个信号。

大户钱包的ETH持仓在悄悄增加，散户在往外跑。这套路我见过——2021年年初就是这样，大户筹码集中度一上来，后面要么走出一波行情，要么就是主力在出货前兆，现在还判断不了。但有一点可以确定：不是散户在买。

交易所净流量最近偏向流入，说明有人在准备卖。配合成交量低迷来看，市场观望情绪重，选择方向前大家都在等。

活跃地址数在下降，但持币超过1年的地址数量在上升。这两件事放一起挺有意思——短期的人在撤，长期的人在等。这是市场在换手，不是抛售。

估值这块，$ 1872离关键支撑$ 1825就差一步。现在市场情绪FNG才29，属于极度恐慌区间的边缘。估值低是真的，但低估不代表马上涨，2018年下半年估值也低，照样阴跌了大半年。

说真的，我现在关心的是高盛这笔收购后续能不能给ETH带来实际的业务增量。如果ETF规模真的做起来，那是大饼ETH都受益的大逻辑。如果只是金融层面的并购整合，短期影响有限。

这种事落到实处，就是看机构的ETF产品能不能真的吸引到钱进来。现在还早，我不下结论。

The just-submitted order for 62,800 got smashed through.

I stared at the screen for two seconds.

My first reaction was to add more to average down.

Wait.

That money is already lost—whether I buy something now has nothing to do with it.

But the human brain doesn’t recognize that logic.

It only remembers how much I put in here, and it can’t bear to let those numbers be wasted.

Today, BTC’s current price is $62,774, down 1.58% over the past 24 hours, with trading volume of only 734 million U.

Low-volume, slow drift lower—there isn’t much sentiment in the market.

But precisely in times like this, it’s easiest to trick yourself with “since I’m already down so much anyway.”

Before adding to your position, ask yourself:

If I were currently in cash with no position, would I still buy at this level?

If the answer is hesitation, don’t let your old position hold your new decision hostage.

What you lose is a sunk cost—not a reason to buy.

Don’t let losses place orders for you.

#BTC #ETH #投资哲学 #交易心态 #crypto circle

Ethereum made a decision that looks like surrender, but is actually very mature.

They spent eight years and poured eight-figure dollars into developing a hashing algorithm specifically designed for zero-knowledge proofs. Yesterday, the Foundation announced: give it up, and switch to SHA and BLAKE—old standards that have been used worldwide for decades.

The reason isn’t that the work failed; it’s that the proof technology itself has advanced, and the older algorithms are now fast enough too. The researchers’ exact words were very precise: the key isn’t “a proof-friendly hash,” but “a hash-friendly proof.”

📌 This is exactly two sides of the same coin as the Coldcard incident I wrote about on August 1—back then, it was a problem with their custom random number generator, and 594 bitcoins were stolen.

You tell me: if eight years of results can be discarded like that, do you think it’s a waste, or a reasonable judgment? Comment and let’s discuss.$ETH $BTC

[History won’t repeat itself exactly, but it always rhymes with the same pattern]

By the end of 2018, ETH had dropped by nearly 90%, and the market was filled with despair. Then in 2019, a doubled-up rally arrived. Back then everyone asked: Did the fundamentals change? No. It only fell far enough that institutions quietly started moving in.

What’s happening now looks painfully familiar.

The FNG index is at 29, staying in the Fear zone consecutively. From the recent high, the price is down 62%—what do you call that? Oversold. With 1825 as support and 1933 as resistance, everything is right there: on the daily and 4H charts, it’s a converging structure; on the 1H chart, a pullback has just finished. On the technical side, this is the standard range-bound base-building setup—low volume, no clear direction, and it’s exhausting.

But looking at charts alone isn’t enough. I’ve never spoken in a way that detached from commercial logic.

Bitmine’s annualized $257 million in staking income, and Goldman Sachs acquiring NEOS to further expand its ETF business—do these signals have weight? I think they do. The first one shows that ETH’s staking model is working and producing real cash flow; the second one shows traditional finance treating ETH as an allocation asset, not just a playground for retail traders.

Is it the same as the end of 2018? Not quite. Back then, we didn’t have these.

This time, the fundamentals are truly changing.

Putting it into concrete terms: big capital is starting to view ETH as an "income-generating asset," not merely a speculative target. Staking yield, ETF allocations, institutional custody—when you put these together, the logic is consistent.

Of course, I’m only saying the logic holds. As for the trading action, this move still needs volume confirmation. As long as 1825 doesn’t break, I lean toward higher probability of an upward move; if it breaks, then the whole judgment has to be redone.

That’s it.

【历史不会简单重复，但总在押同样的韵脚】

2018年底，ETH跌了快90%，市场一片绝望，结果2019年迎 来了一波翻倍行情。那时候大家也问：基本面变了吗？没有。只是跌透了，机构开始悄悄进场。

现在的情形，我看着眼熟得很。

FNG指数29，连续在Fear区间，价格从高点下来跌了62%，这叫什么？这叫超跌。1825支撑、1933阻力，摆在那儿，日线4H都是收敛结构，1H刚走完一波回调。技术面上，这是标准的震荡筑底图形——没量，没方向，磨人。

但光看图不够，我讲东西从来不脱离商业逻辑。

Bitmine年化2.57亿美金的质押收入，高盛收购NEOS加码ETF业务，这两个信号你说有没有分量？我看有。前一个说明ETH的Staking模式跑通了，有真实现金流；后一个说明传统金融在拿ETH当资产配置，不再只是散户在玩。

这跟2018年底一样吗？不一样。那时候没有这些。这次是基本面真的在变。

落到实处的意思就是——大资金开始把ETH当"能产生收益的资产"看了，不只是投机标的。质押收益、ETF配置、机构托管，这几个东西组合在一起，逻辑是通的。

当然，我只是说逻辑通。盘面上，这波还需要放量确认。1825不破，我倾向向上概率大；破了，整个判断要重新来过。
